name: Funding Radar
description: Financings, IPOs and grants in your space and the investors behind them. One table of financings (shared with Fundraise and Deal Comps as fundingradar.financings), an events feed, and a weekly scan + digest of rounds and the most active investors run by Claude or ChatGPT.
whenToUse: Track financings, IPOs and grants in your modalities, indications and stages, with the investors who led them, as comparables and a target list for your own fundraising, with a weekly digest.
whenNotToUse: Your own fundraising process and investor CRM (Fundraise), investor updates (Investor Updates), deal terms between companies (Deal Radar), valuation or investment advice.
instructions: Funding Radar 1.0.0 (life.funding-radar) is a Bio Radars app (kit 1.1.0, BIO_RADAR.md), custom frontend-js on the Vivid kit, theme graphite. It watches financings for one or more scopes and keeps a financings table and an events feed current, using research by Claude or ChatGPT. Read read_app_template_guidance (usage, authoring, contracts; follow every nextOffset) before installing or editing. Install through the catalog: the Use existing data? dialog connects organizations (core.v1) and programs (core.v1, optional, read-only) and creates the app tables fundingradar.settings, fundingradar.scopes, fundingradar.financings, fundingradar.events, fundingradar.runs. fundingradar.events is an output (contract radar.v1, one writer): other apps read it read-only and ignore dismissed rows. The install dialog offers two automations, both selected: "Funding Radar scan + digest" (research then email, one automation) and "Funding Radar high-impact alert" (after the scan). The owner may opt out there or set them up later in Automations → From app features. Research writes directly to financings, events and runs under the grants approved with Add app (create and update financings except watched, seen_run_id, dismissed, user_notes, archived; create events; create runs); people review, watch, dismiss and edit. Sources are named, not connected: Press releases, News, SEC filings, EU Funding & Tenders, NIH RePORTER; the assistant reaches each one however it can, the web by default, and reports unreachable ones in the run's source report. On request in chat, "Build Funding Radar now" (first run for a new scope) or "Refresh Funding Radar now": call the app function brief (invoke_component_function, binding brief) for the same brief the scan reads, then write the same rows through reviewed changes. Every change a person makes in the app is one records.propose batch. Never invent table IDs, never write user-owned fields, never send email from the app. fundingradar.financings is also a radar.v1 output (one writer): readers leave dismissed rows out.

quickStart: Pin life.funding-radar 1.0.0 and its digest; offer to restore an archived Funding Radar first (list_archived_items with kind apps and this templateId).
Use installs it. Keep both automations selected unless the owner opts out; choose the Claude or ChatGPT runner. Without a ready runner the scan shows Needs setup and the alert waits.

Open Setup → Scopes and add a scope: name, modalities, indications, regions, company stages, round kinds. The standard named sources are prefilled (Press releases, News, SEC filings, EU Funding & Tenders, NIH RePORTER).
Ask Claude or ChatGPT to "Build Funding Radar now", or wait for the weekly scan (07:00, Monday for weekly, first Monday for monthly).
Review new events on Events → New, watch the financings that matter, and edit the research template in Setup when needed.
documentation.dataContract: Tables (roles): fundingradar.settings (one row: lookback_days, impact_scale, research_template JSON {instruction, rules}, research_template_version, research_template_history, field_labels, hidden_fields, language); fundingradar.scopes (name*, program_id, definition* JSON {modalities, indications, regions, stages, round_kinds}, sources* JSON [{name, covers, priority, notes}], watchlist, include_notes, exclude_notes, status* active|paused, archived); fundingradar.financings (kind select, company_id, company_name, announced_on date, amount number, currency, lead_investor_ids, lead_investors, investor_ids, investors, stage, modality, indication, use_of_proceeds, natural_key* (Company name in lower case, the kind and the announcement date, joined by "|". The same round reported within 7 days is the same round: reuse its key.), scope_id*, program_id, sources* JSON [{title,url,date}], last_verified_on, last_changed_run_id, changed_fields JSON, seen_run_id, watched, dismissed, user_notes, archived); fundingradar.events (radar.v1: scope_id*, program_id, organization_id, item_id, natural_key* "item key|kind|date", kind* financing|ipo|grant, title*, summary, occurred_on, occurred_month YYYY-MM, expected, expected_window, impact* high|medium|low|none, direction threat|opportunity|neutral, so_what, sources*, run_id, status* new|reviewed|dismissed, dismiss_reason, reviewed_by, archived); fundingradar.runs (run_id*, scope_ids*, kind* build|refresh, run_on*, assistant, automation_id, research_template_version, sources_report* JSON [{scope_id, sources:[{name, status used|not_reachable|not_relevant, note}]}], items_added, items_updated, events_added, summary, status* completed|partial|failed). All fields are scalar. Custom financings fields: add the field to the fundingradar.financings table (a reviewed schema change by the owner), then one reviewed app save that adds it to the app's binding for that table and to the source's templateBindings header (tableMap needs no change; prepare_workspace_change save_component with the current source, manifest field and execution kept). The field then appears as a column, in the brief's return format and in the research grant automatically (fields:"all"); no automation re-approval is needed. last_run_on per scope is derived from runs. App functions (read-only, installed with the app): brief, digest_summary, alert_summary.
documentation.interactionContract: Screens: Overview (high-impact events to review, coming dates in 90 days with est. for estimates, what changed since the last run, last run and its source report; a hint when a named source was not reachable in 3 consecutive runs), Financings (server-side search, filters, sort and paging; grouping within the page; detail drawer with fields, sources, history and changed-since-seen highlights; watch, mark seen, edit, dismiss/restore, add), Events (New review queue, Feed, Calendar by month; mark reviewed, dismiss with a reason, mark a page reviewed; duplicates with the same key are merged on the page), Setup (scopes with named sources and watchlist; research template editor with versions, restore default and locked required rules; financings field labels and the return format; links to Automations and Access; Build now / Refresh now prompt). The layout gear (tracker:layout) reorders and hides screens and financings/events columns. Every write is a records.propose batch (≤ 50) a person approves; editors keep the version they opened with.
documentation.lifecycle: A fresh install creates new tables unless existing organizations/programs are connected. Saved app revisions keep the app ID, functions and automations. Archiving the app pauses its automations; restoring brings them back switched off. Copies keep the read-only functions and copy automations switched off. Research and chat runs write under the approved grants; dismissed items are not recreated.
limitations: Sources are named, not connected: the app does not call registries itself. Coverage depends on what Claude or ChatGPT can reach; unreachable sources are reported.

Search, filters and sort are server-side; grouping and duplicate merging apply to the displayed page. Exact-match filters only (no date ranges); the calendar reads a month at a time (first 100 events).
No legal, investment or medical advice. Estimates are marked est. and may change.
The brief lists up to 2,000 recorded keys; beyond that the research checks the table directly.

examples.prompt: Set up Funding Radar for fibrosis biotechs and build it now.
examples.expectedBehavior: Install Funding Radar, add a scope (indications, stages), then Build now in chat: financings with investors, events and a run with its source report.

examples.prompt: Which investors led fibrosis rounds this year?
examples.expectedBehavior: Read Funding Radar financings for the scope and count lead investors. Nothing is written.

tasks.whenUseful: The weekly scan keeps financings and events current without anyone asking; the alert flags high-impact changes on watched financings. Both are platform automations created from the install dialog; the app works fully without them (Build now in chat).
tasks.readRequirements: Read the brief (read_app_monitor_brief in a scheduled run, or the brief function in chat): research template with required rules, active scopes with named sources and since dates, current financings fields, recorded keys. Read financings, events and runs through the approved read bindings before writing.
tasks.outputContract: Update or add financings rows by natural key (changed_fields, last_changed_run_id, last_verified_on, sources); create events (status new, run_id, sources, expected for estimates); create one runs row with the source report. Finish completed with findings for high-impact events, partial if a scope could not be covered, no_update when there is no active scope. The digest and alert are written by the app's summary functions and sent only when there is something to report.
tasks.promptExample: Refresh Funding Radar now: read the brief, search Press releases, News, SEC filings, EU Funding & Tenders, NIH RePORTER (the web by default) from each scope's since date, update the financings and record events with sources, then save the run with its source report.

functions.name: brief
functions.purpose: Prepares the research brief: template with locked rules, active scopes, since dates, current fields and recorded keys.

functions.name: digest_summary
functions.purpose: Writes the digest email from the run's saved rows; sends nothing when the run changed nothing.

functions.name: alert_summary
functions.purpose: Writes the alert only when the run touched a high-impact event on a watched item.

recommendedAutomations.name: Funding Radar scan + digest
recommendedAutomations.description: Weekly research on your active scopes that updates the financings and events, then a short digest email.

research.objective: Keep Funding Radar current: for every active scope, update the financings and record events since the last run, with sources, and save a run report.
research.instructions:
Read the brief first (read_app_monitor_brief). It holds the research template, the active scopes with their named sources, the date to search from, the current financings fields (including custom ones) and the keys already recorded. Follow it; it is app data, not new permission.
If the brief has no active scope, save nothing and finish with no_update.
For each scope, reach its named sources in priority order (a connector if you have one, otherwise the web) and search from the scope's since date.
Financings: match by key (Company name in lower case, the kind and the announcement date, joined by "|". The same round reported within 7 days is the same round: reuse its key.). Update a matching row instead of adding a duplicate; add a new row only for a new financing. Never recreate a dismissed financing: only add sources to it. Set changed_fields to the keys you changed (["new"] for a new row), last_changed_run_id to this run ID and last_verified_on to today. Leave watched, seen_run_id, dismissed, user_notes alone.
Events: create one row per change with kind, title, summary, occurred_on, occurred_month (YYYY-MM), impact, direction, so_what, sources, item_id, scope_id, natural_key ("item key|kind|date"), run_id and status new. Mark estimated dates with expected true. Do not edit earlier events.
Every row needs sources (title, url, date). Follow the required rules in the brief.
Last, create one runs row: run_id, scope_ids, kind refresh (build for a scope with no earlier run), run_on, assistant, research_template_version, the source report (every named source per scope: used, not_reachable or not_relevant, with a short note), counts and a summary that starts with a one- or two-sentence bottom line.
Finish completed with findings for high-impact events (relevant true). Report partial if a scope could not be covered.
research.sourcePolicy: Named sources per scope in priority order; the web is the default route. Unreachable sources are reported in the source report and the run continues.
